sections.kicker: Prepared for Karlie Reitano by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Karlie Reitano has a personality that fills a sentence and a site that gives it a stock photo.
sections.keep: The handwritten signature logo. It is the one element that is only hers.

pins.quote: PR & Marketing Consultant, Storyteller, Brand Cheerleader,
pins.what: Four titles stack in one sentence.
pins.why: Consultant, storyteller, cheerleader and hype woman each describe a different job, and none says what she is the best at.
pins.how: Pick the one title a client would hire her for and let the rest become her tone.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: A founder looking for a publicist cannot tell which one she is hiring.

pins.area: A blue-tinted photo of blurred people on a stone staircase behind the headline
pins.what: The hero is a blue-tinted photo of strangers on a staircase.
pins.why: It is the kind of image any agency in any city could use, and it has no trace of her warmth.
pins.how: Replace it with something only her work or her clients could have made.
pins.label: Your hero photo
pins.cost: The first image says that she could be anyone.

pins.what: The menu says join our team under a name and a tagline that say for hire.
pins.why: One voice is a solo consultant and the other is an agency, and a new client has to guess which they are getting.
pins.how: Decide whether the brand is her or a team, and let the language follow.
pins.label: Your menu
pins.cost: The scale of the business is unclear before anyone has talked to her.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Karlie Reitano's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Glossier, from another category. It started as one voice talking directly to one person and never lost it.
